newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope calls for end to child prostitution.
newsitem.headline: Pope calls for end to child prostitution.

text.p: Pope John Paul called on Friday for a concerted international effort to end child prostitution and put a stop to recent growth in sex tourism in Asia.

The Pope told representatives of the lobby group End Child Prostitution in Asian Tourism during an audience at the Vatican that extreme poverty and lack of adequate social structures in Asian countries forced many children into prostitution.
"Only concerted action by national and international institutions, by associations and individuals, can put an end to this very serious social plague," the Pope said.
The dignity of millions of children was being trodden upon and their future was being stolen, he added.
Recent growth in organised sex tourism was a product of a decline in moral standards and family values in the world's developed nations, he said.

"In richer countries...a hedonistic vision of life can destroy moral standards, justifying anything if it gives pleasure," he said, "In this context how can we not see in pornography an incitement to this type of abuse."

Organisations fighting the spread of sex tourism in Asia have focused their campaigns on Thailand and the Philippines but now say other less developed countries in the region such as Cambodia and Laos are also at risk.
